content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am encountering an issue when attempting to use a USB cable to transfer my projects to the [product_name]. The software cannot connect to COM 1. System details: - Running [product_name] [product_name] V[version_no] on Windows 10 - Have a [article_no] [product_name] - Have a [article_no] USB PC-to-[product_name] cable - Official drivers installed from the V[version_no] download The cable functions correctly on my older XP workstation with [product_name] V[version_no], but IT requires me to move to Windows 10 as XP is no longer supported. Thank you in advance for any assistance. [user_name]
Submit a support request for further help.

Hello, Open your system's control panel and navigate to device manager. Check the section for "Connections COM & LPT." Next, plug in the USB cable and look for the COM port number assigned. This is the COM port you must select for connecting to the [product_name] using the USB programming cable. If no new COM port is shown, try uninstalling a device with a COM port under COM10 and repeat the process. Sometimes virtual COM port handling in Windows can be unpredictable. Also, avoid using the cable via a USB port replicator. I hope this helps.

Hello, I regularly use both the older USB serial interface and newer Ethernet options. Windows may change the COM address for the USB/serial driver, which can cause issues. Go to device manager, locate the correct COM port for the serial interface, and avoid non-powered USB hubs for better reliability. When using the [product_name] software, select the [product_name] cable interface and choose the corresponding COM port. This issue arises from how Windows manages legacy serial ports. Personally, I use one dedicated USB port on my laptop for the serial interface to avoid COM port resets.
